A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, Referring to Any Person, with 17 readable pages including five supplementary pages. Full-text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable comparison of the text, tables, figures, equations, and appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original HumanRef benchmark experiments, rejection-data and training-stage ablations, and RexSeek generalization results on RefCOCOg in Tables 4 and 6–8.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark, ablation, and generalization results, including the numerical outcomes in Tables 4 and 6–8.

M1.justification: Section 4 and supplementary Section 8 describe the same RexSeek architecture, box-index retrieval procedure, and four-stage training. No algorithmic component or training objective changes.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation coverage is unchanged. Table 8's caption changes from RefCOCO/+/g to RefCOCOg, but its columns and the experiment description already identified RefCOCOg in v1; this corrects labeling rather than removes benchmarks.

E2.justification: The comparator rows in Tables 4 and 8 and the model series in Figure 7 are identical. No comparison method is added, removed, or replaced.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, sample counts, model configurations, training settings, and evaluation procedures are unchanged, including the IoU and point-in-mask criteria in Section 5.1. The Table 8 caption correction does not establish a changed experimental setting.

E4.justification: The rejection-data ablation in Table 6, training-stage ablation in Table 7, instance-count analysis in Figure 7, and general-object examples in Figure 8 are unchanged. The appendices add no new analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Statistical uncertainty reporting is unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical results, plotted trends, and qualitative examples are unchanged. For example, RexSeek retains average HumanRef DensityF1 of 82.3 in Table 4 and RefCOCOg validation/test scores of 84.0/84.4 in Table 8.

T1.justification: The task definitions, architecture equations, and DensityF1 definition and penalty in Equations 1–2 are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion are unchanged. Both versions claim the same task formulation, HumanRef dataset contribution, and RexSeek capabilities for human and general-object referring.

C2.justification: Explanations of low multi-instance recall, hallucination, training-stage benefits, and generalization remain identical, as does the qualification about point-based versus box-based evaluation. No substantive interpretation or limitation is added.

D1.justification: The supplementary annotation prompts, encoder specifications, input resolutions, batch sizes, and learning rates are unchanged. Code-access information and linked destinations also remain identical.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and all 85 references are unchanged, including the positioning relative to ChatRex and existing referring-expression datasets.

P1.justification: Table 4 changes the category heading Property to Attribute, and Table 8 corrects its caption's dataset name to RefCOCOg. Apart from the arXiv version/date stamp, there are no other textual changes or structural revisions.

P2.justification: The Table 4 heading and Table 8 caption are edited, with slight line reflow in the latter. Figures, table structures, placements, and appendix layouts are otherwise unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves reporting accuracy: Table 8's caption now matches its RefCOCOg columns, and Table 4 uses the established Attribute terminology. These corrections reduce ambiguity without changing evidence or methods. The benefit is limited, particularly because Section 5.3 still describes Table 8's performance using the broader RefCOCO/+/g wording.
